extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and recipient institutions for NIH construction/modernization grants and Kirschstein-NRSA (individual fellowship) applicants and their sponsoring institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for (1) construction, modernization, and major alteration/renovation (A&R) projects funded by NIH (environmental, statutory, executive order, procurement, closeout, and real property requirements) and (2) Kirschstein-NRSA individual fellowship eligibility, sponsorship, application, and award conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seismic safety (Earthquake Hazards Reduction Act / EO 12699)
rubrics_metrics.description: New federally assisted or regulated buildings must be designed and constructed using appropriate seismic standards compliant with State, county, or local jurisdictional building ordinances; special structural and other features to protect life and minimize damage (including tornado protections) may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to NIH-assisted construction located in applicable geographic locations; follow EO 12699 and applicable State/local building ordinances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endangered Species Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must comply with the Endangered Species Act for the protection of endangered species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposed activities may affect listed species or critical habitat, NIH will take into account those effects before approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flood Disaster Protection Act / Flood Insurance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: No Federal financial assistance for acquisition, modernization, or construction of property may be provided in identified flood-prone communities unless the community participates in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and flood insurance is purchased within 1 year of the identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists of flood-prone areas eligible for flood insurance are published by FEMA in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead-based paint prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits the use of lead-based paint in construction or rehabilitation of residence structures (Lead-Based Paint Poisoning Prevention Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure materials and construction practices avoid lead-based paint where statute applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA environmental review and reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Because construction/modernization/major A&R can affect the environment, applicants must provide information on anticipated environmental impact as part of their just-in-time submission; applicants may use the Review of Environmental and Other Impacts document or an equivalent format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will review submitted information and determine whether an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS), Environmental Assessment (EA), or No Further Action is required. If EA/EIS is required, the applicant (recipient) must conduct the appropriate environmental review and provide necessary documentation to NIH for review, approval, and processing. NIH will advise and make final environmental determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide permits, licenses, and planning authority consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide a current listing and copies, as applicable, of all relevant licenses, permits, and other approvals required (including State and local air, water quality, and zoning board reports) and indicate the State, local, and regional planning authorities contacted or consulted regarding the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly discuss the proposed facility with respect to regional development plans. Applicants are not required to incur costs for extensive consultant services at the application stage; hiring consultants to develop detailed data/elaborate presentations is discouraged and such costs generally will not be allowable as pre-award costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA Public disclosure and public participation (Section 102 / EO 11514)
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is an environmental impact (in accord with NEPA), the applicant must publicly disclose the project in a newspaper or other publicly available medium and describe any environmental impacts concurrent with notification to the SPOC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a disclosure statement (sample provided in guidance) and allow public comment or requests for information concerning environmental implications; address communications to the institutional office specified and give a deadline for comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic preservation clearance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the National Historic Preservation Act and the Archaeological and Historic Preservation Act, before approval of a grant-related activity NIH must take into account the effect on properties in the National Register of Historic Places or those eligible for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an eligible or potentially eligible historic property will be affected, the applicant must obtain clearance from the appropriate State Historic Preservation Office and Tribal Historic Preservation Office before submitting the application; failure to obtain clearance will delay NIH action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility under Rehabilitation Act Section 504
rubrics_metrics.description: Each facility or part of a facility constructed, modernized, or altered shall be designed and constructed so that it is readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons; modernization or alterations that affect usability must, to the maximum extent feasible, make the altered portion accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design, construction, or alteration of buildings shall conform to Federal Property Management Regulations at 41 CFR Part 102 subchapter C, Real Property, Part 102-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe Drinking Water Act applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Title XIV of the Public Health Service Act (Safe Drinking Water Act) applies to the protection of underground sources of drinking water for NIH-supported construction or modernization activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects that cause displacement must comply with the Uniform Relocation Act (49 CFR Part 24). HHS requirements reference these regulations and provide policies and procedures for acquisition of real property and require that displaced people be treated fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow applicable HHS/NIH implementing regulations (45 CFR Part 15 referencing 49 CFR Part 24). Encourage early, prompt, amicable negotiation to protect property owners’ interests and avoid litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wild and Scenic Rivers Act consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect components or potential components of the national wild and scenic rivers system when project activities may affect these resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intergovernmental review under EO 12372 (SPOC process)
rubrics_metrics.description: EO 12372 requires consultation with State and local officials on certain proposed Federal assistance. NIH construction and modernization grants are subject to these requirements for states that participate in the intergovernmental review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from participating states should contact their SPOC early, provide a copy of the application to the SPOC no later than the time of submission to NIH, and submit SPOC comments with the application or indicate the date provided to the SPOC. SPOCs are given 60 days to review. If comments are not submitted with the application, provide them upon receipt and may include applicant's reaction, or notify NIH that no SPOC response was received. Indian tribes are not subject to these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floodplain management (EO 11988)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid uneconomical, hazardous, or unnecessary use of flood plains for construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess floodplain implications in accordance with EO 11988 and applicable NIH/agency procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Wetlands (EO 11990)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider protection of wetlands in project planning and approvals in accordance with EO 11990.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric system usage (EO 12770)
rubrics_metrics.description: All construction, modernization, or A&R (major or minor) supported by NIH grant funds must be designed using the metric system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design documentation and specifications should use metric units consistent with EO 12770.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching funds requirement (as specified in NOFO/NoA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching requirements, when applicable, are specified in the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and the Notice of Award (NoA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific NOFO/NoA for matching obligations and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Design Requirements Manual and Design Documentation Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH design requirements and design documentation requirements apply to projects as specified (applicable or specified in the NOFO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the NIH Design Requirements Manual and NOFO for applicable documentation expectations and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement requirements for construction grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement rules and requirements apply to NIH-funded construction, modernization, and A&R activities as specified by NIH and applicable Federal regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procurement provisions spelled out in the NOFO/NoA and relevant Federal regulations (e.g., 2 CFR Part 200 procurement standards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidated damages applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Liquidated damages provisions are applicable to construction, modernization, and major A&R projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the NOFO/contract documents for specific liquidated damages clauses and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Employment Opportunity and Labor Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal Employment Opportunity requirements and labor standards apply to construction and modernization grants and major A&R projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with EEO and labor standards provisions referenced in the NOFO and applicable statutes/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards (contracts > $100,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards apply to contracts exceeding $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contracts include required clauses and that payroll and hours requirements are met for covered contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of Unclaimed Wages
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions for disposition of unclaimed wages apply to construction-related contracts and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real property management standards (notice of Federal interest, title insurance, physical destruction insurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Real property management standards apply, including requirements for notice of Federal interest and title insurance; physical destruction insurance is applicable unless waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NOFO/NoA and 2 CFR/45 CFR provisions addressing real property management, insurance, and Federal interest notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of facility and disposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of facility and disposition requirements are specified in the NOFO/NoA or in 2 CFR Part 200.311 and 45 CFR Part 75.318 and/or as specified by NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult NOFO/NoA and applicable regulations for restrictions, required uses, and disposition procedures at closeout or when property is no longer used for the award purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout: final record as-built construction documents
rubrics_metrics.description: At closeout, final record as-built construction documents are required for construction grants (applicable), for modernization grants (applicable), and may be N/A for certain major A&R projects as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit complete as-built documentation per NOFO/NIH closeout instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kirschstein-NRSA authority and payback requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirschstein-NRSA individual fellowships support predoctoral and postdoctoral training; the legislation requires postdoctoral NRSA recipients to 'pay back' to the Federal government their initial 12 months of Kirschstein-NRSA postdoctoral support by engaging in health-related biomedical, behavioral and/or clinical research, health-related research training, health-related teaching, or any combination of these activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Payback Requirements section for details on fulfillment and certification obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination and assurance filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kirschstein-NRSA program is conducted in compliance with applicable laws prohibiting discrimination (race, color, national origin, handicap, age, sex as applicable). Applicant organizations are required to have appropriate Assurance of Compliance forms filed with HHS’s Office for Civil Rights (OCR) before a grant may be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the NIH awarding IC if there are questions concerning compliance. See Public Policy Requirements and Objectives—Civil Rights in IIA for detailed requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible research areas (must fall within NIH IC missions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships may be made for research training in areas that fall within the missions of the NIH Institutes and Centers (ICs). Applications that do not address these areas will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult specific IC mission statements and the NOFO; there is an increased emphasis on training physicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of funds for research training (vs. clinical degrees/residency)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kirschstein-NRSA fellowship must be used to support a program of research training. It may not support studies leading to clinical professional degrees (M.D., D.O., D.D.S., etc.) except when those studies are part of a formal combined research degree program (e.g., M.D./Ph.D.). Fellowships may not support the clinical portion of residency training. Research fellows in clinical areas are expected to devote full time effort to the proposed research training and to confine clinical duties to those that are part of the research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postdoctoral fellows proposing training at their doctoral institution must document thoroughly the opportunity for new training experiences designed to broaden scientific backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree requirements for predoctoral, postdoctoral, and senior fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: Predoctoral: must have a baccalaureate degree and be enrolled in a program leading to a Ph.D. or equivalent research degree. Postdoctoral: must have a doctoral degree (Ph.D., M.D., D.D.S., etc.) before award activation. Senior fellows: must have a doctoral degree and at least 7 subsequent years of relevant research and professional experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable degrees and equivalency statements are specified; sponsoring institution is responsible for determining foreign degree equivalence. Senior fellowship is full-time and intended for experienced scientists to change or broaden research directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / permanent residency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals must be U.S. citizens, noncitizen nationals, or have been lawfully admitted for permanent residence by time of award. Applicants expecting permanent residency by earliest award date may apply, but notarized documentation of admission for permanent residence is required prior to award. Individuals on temporary or student visas are not eligible unless they have begun the permanent residency process and expect admission by the earliest possible award date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permanent Resident Card (USCIS Form I-551) or other legal verification required; sponsoring institution is responsible for follow-up if validation is time-limited. Conditional permanent residents and asylum/refugee applicants have specific considerations; check guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship and sponsoring institution responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must identify a sponsoring institution and an individual sponsor (mentor) who will supervise training and research. The sponsoring institution is legally responsible for providing facilities and financially responsible for the use and disposition of funds. The sponsor should be an active investigator who documents the training plan, availability of staff, research support, and facilities for high-quality research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postdoctoral applicants proposing training at their doctoral institution must demonstrate new training opportunities. Foreign sponsorship requires detailed justification comparing scientific advantages to domestic training, may need additional administrative reviews, and will be considered only when scientific advantages are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal employees / NIH employees as applicants (Federal Fellows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil service employees and PHS commissioned officers at NIH and other Federal laboratories may compete for predoctoral and postdoctoral fellowships, but proposed training should be primarily for career development rather than immediate research needs of NIH or the Federal lab. An individual supported under a fellowship may not also hold an employee position with the Federal Government at activation of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When at an NIH laboratory, the employee’s supervisor must disassociate themselves from review and award processes. Successful applicants must resign or take leave without pay (LWOP) prior to activating the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuals on active military duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Career military personnel may apply while on active duty; the military branch should submit a letter endorsing the application and indicating willingness to continue normal active duty pay and allowances during the fellowship period. NIH will pay institutional allowance and tuition/fees when permitted, but stipends, health insurance, and travel allowances are not allowable charges to an NRSA fellowship for career military personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of concurrent benefits by NIH to active-duty career military recipients is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application package and emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship applications must be submitted electronically through Grants.gov using the application package provided in the NOFO (combines SF424 (R&R) and PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form). The major emphasis of the application should be the research training experience and broadening of scientific competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) secures and retains assurance signatures. Postdoctoral applicants must certify they have read the payback information. Applicants and institutions must comply with policies on civil rights, human subjects protection, research misconduct, animal care, inclusion, stem cells, recombinant nucleic molecules, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons registration and PI Role assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: All fellowship applicants and sponsoring institutions must be registered in the eRA Commons. The fellowship applicant must be assigned the 'PI Role' in the eRA Commons to access application and review information. Applicants submitting through a different sponsoring institution must be affiliated with that sponsoring institution in eRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional and individual eRA Commons registrations are complete well before submission deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID iD requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: ORCID identifiers are required and enforced at the time of application for specified individual fellowship activity codes (F05, F30, F31, F32, F33, F37, F38, F99/K00, F12). eRA system validations will check whether applicants have ORCID iDs and applications will not be accepted unless an ORCID iD is linked to the PD/PI's eRA Commons Personal Profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should link or create ORCID accounts and link them to eRA Commons prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At least three (but no more than five) letters of reference must be submitted on behalf of the fellowship applicant. Reference letters are submitted directly by referees through the eRA Commons and are joined with the application once submission completes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missing required letters may delay review or lead to non-acceptance. Applicants must follow instructions in the Individual Fellowship Application Guide and provide referees with the specific instructions.
